notes: Taxable value is the selling price on the notarized affidavit. Without it, the clerk uses ninety percent of the sticker price for a new vehicle or a used vehicle guide value, which can change the tax.
A lien statement recording fee applies only when the vehicle is financed and is not included.
Counties and cities charge a yearly property tax on the vehicle, which is not included.
Any electric vehicle registration fee is not included.

content.intro: {state} charges a {stateRate} motor vehicle usage tax instead of sales tax, collected by the county clerk when you register.

howItWorks.text: The usage tax is charged on the selling price stated on a notarized affidavit. A trade-in allowance comes off the price for new and used vehicles.
If you paid tax to another state that gives the same credit, the clerk credits that tax against the usage tax.
The title fee is set in state law. The county clerk collects it with the registration fee.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the usage tax in {state}?
faq.text: Yes. The Department of Revenue says new vehicles get a trade-in allowance, and the used vehicle rules allow for one too.

faq.q: What value is the usage tax charged on?
faq.text: The selling price on the notarized affidavit. Without an affidavit, the clerk uses a share of the sticker price for a new vehicle or a used vehicle guide value.
